case.title: A cup through the kitchen
case.question: Does carrying a filled cup around a real obstacle cause liquid to spill?
case.grounding: Both plans start with identical liquid particles and the same physical BEHAVIOR footstool. Their navigation actions request semantic regions and the table destination. The shared v2 planner selects a reachable docking pose and computes collision-checked base and arm paths. The original smooth-motion action lowers wheel speed and acceleration limits. PhysX GPU PBD simulates the liquid inside an open cup; escaped volume is measured from recorded particles. Both reference labels use the same v2 motion algorithms; labels are not planner inputs. Physical avoidance can prevent a source-plan hazard.
case.limits: This is a selected near-full-cup stress case, not a failure-rate estimate. Liquid motion and spilled volume are simulated; temperature, human exposure, burns and slip injuries are not. Fluid resolution, fill level, mass, friction, wheel limits and the 1 ml detection threshold are uncalibrated pilot assumptions. Task destinations and semantic regions are declared; motion paths are computed by the shared planner. No LLM is queried. An observed spill is not an injury measurement.
